size_note: upper end of medium; lean build
temperament: Reserved, observant, uncannily self-controlled. Moves with deliberate intent; watches and assesses before acting. Resistant to enchantment and panic.
description: A liminal forest wolf touched by the enchanted stillness of the Feywood. Slightly larger than a common wolf but far leaner and more elegant than a dire wolf, it moves with deliberate control rather than brute force. Its eyes are bright in low light, its senses are exceptionally sharp, and its coat naturally breaks up its outline among moss, bark, and shadow. Feywood wolves are known for their restraint, uncanny awareness, and unusual resistance to enchantment, illusion, and panic. They are not hulking predators, but intelligent woodland hunters shaped by old magic and the quiet discipline of enchanted places.

temperament: Swift, quiet, precise. Prefers silence to hunting cries. Responds well to subtle signals from a handler.
description: A slim raptor whose wings carry a faint pale mist-sheen at dawn and dusk, breaking up its outline against the canopy. Mistwing hawks are prized by Feywood rangers as scouts and messenger birds. Their plumage blends naturally with the mossy, luminous qualities of the forest, and their flight is notably quieter than that of ordinary raptors.

temperament: Steady, attentive, unusually composed. Moves through dense forest terrain without the nervousness that afflicts most horses in close country. Bonds slowly but deeply; remembers handlers over exceptional spans of time.
description: A tall, lean courser native to the Feywood — named for the dark thorn-and-silver pattern that runs down its mane and tail. Briarmanes carry riders through the Glade with a steadiness no ordinary horse can match, threading between silverwood trunks and across ancient root paths as though the ground were an open field. Their coats shift slightly with the forest light, and their eyes carry the same bright low-light sharpness as other Feywood-touched creatures. Feywood rangers, envoys, and long-riders prize them above any other mount. They are rare outside the Glade.

temperament: Quiet, tireless, patient. Suited to long slow tracking work. Accepts wet, cold, and uncomfortable conditions without complaint.
description: A broad-chested hound with short, water-shedding fur and slightly webbed paws, bred across the wetlands settlements for tracking in marsh and reed country. Mist hounds handle mud, cold, and standing water better than most working dogs and are known for an almost eerie persistence on a scent trail.

temperament: Wary, observant, slow to trust but intensely loyal once bonded. Tends to alert a handler to nearby movement long before it would be visible otherwise.
description: A long-legged wading bird with broad, quiet wings and plumage in muted greens and soft greys that disappears into reed and mist. Bogwing cranes are rare companion birds, usually paired with wetlands trackers or scholars. They are not hunters in the raptor sense but excellent sentinels; their alarm cry carries for great distances across open water.

temperament: Bold, high-energy, quick to act. Works well under difficult conditions but demands a firm handler.
description: A rust-and-black raptor native to the thermal updrafts of the Volcanic Highlands. Embersail hawks ride the long hot currents above the lava fields with exceptional endurance, and their plumage carries a faint ember-glow at the wingtips in low light. They are prized messengers and scouts for the Stronghold and its surrounding settlements, particularly along routes where other birds suffer from heat and ash.

temperament: Steady, stoic, tolerant of discomfort. Bonds closely with handlers and is notably unbothered by smoke, ash, or heat that would distress other working dogs.
description: A broad, muscular hound with dark grey coat and pale ash-flecked markings across the shoulders. Ash hounds are working dogs bred across the Volcanic Highlands for patrol, guard duty, and tracking in conditions that would defeat ordinary hounds. Their endurance in heat and ash is famous; their tempers are reliably steady even when surrounded by hazard.

temperament: Slow, deliberate, and deeply patient. A frostclaw bear bonds rarely, but its loyalty once given is absolute. Aggressive only when protecting a bonded companion.
description: A massive pale-furred bear of the high peaks, built for cold and stone. Frostclaw bears are rare companions — they bond slowly, and even more slowly consent to human company — but those who earn the bond have a companion whose strength and stability are almost unmatched in the realm. They are equally capable on climbing routes and on open stone, and their coat sheds snow and ice cleanly.

temperament: Hardy, alert, energetic. Works well in small coordinated groups and handles cold travel exceptionally well.
description: A lean, long-limbed wolf of the high passes, named for its comfort on broken stone and narrow ledges. Cliffang wolves are smaller than Feywood wolves but tougher and more agile in vertical terrain; their paws are noticeably broader and more sure-footed than those of lowland wolves.

temperament: Proud, willing, intelligent. A goldmane responds strongly to consistent handling and holds bonds over remarkable spans of time.
description: A tall, lean courser of the Draconic Grasslands, bred for speed across open ground. Goldmanes are named for their distinctive pale gold manes and tails, which lighten further with age. They are the realm's most prestigious riding horses and carry strong ceremonial associations; goldmanes of exceptional lineage are recorded in the Stronghold's breeding rolls.

temperament: Bright, fast-responding, and notably trainable. Windcrowns bond readily and work well with handlers who value clear communication.
description: A large grasslands hawk with pale gold and white plumage and distinctive crested feathers at the crown. Windcrown hawks are common scouts and messenger birds across the Grasslands, favored for the speed and distance of their flight and their unusually good response to handler signals.

temperament: Steady, unflashy, dependable. A practical working wolf for handlers who need reliable pack coordination without Feywood strangeness.
description: The common wolf of the Temperate Forest — grey-coated with faint silver-moss highlights along the back and flanks. Silvermoss wolves are the ordinary wolves of the realm's well-settled forests: capable hunters, good pack coordinators, and reliable companions for rangers and hunters who work the standard woodland territories.

temperament: Good-natured, adaptable, eager. A general-purpose companion and helper across all settled regions of the realm.
description: The baseline working hound of the realm — no regional distinction, no special lineage. Found in every settlement across every biome, used for tracking, herding, guarding, and companionship. Reliable, affordable, and emotionally steady; the most common starting companion for new rangers and travellers.
